discovery: Cosmic inflation and the quantum origin of cosmic structure
motivation: Guth proposed that an early epoch of accelerated expansion explains the flatness and horizon problems. Linde developed viable new and chaotic inflationary scenarios. Mukhanov (with the late Chibisov) showed that quantum vacuum fluctuations stretched during inflation seed all cosmic structure, predicting adiabatic, Gaussian, nearly scale-invariant perturbations with a small red tilt. Three decades of CMB measurements, culminating in WMAP and Planck, have confirmed these predictions quantitatively: superhorizon adiabatic correlations shown by the TE polarization cross-spectrum, Gaussianity at the 10^-4 level, spatial flatness to better than 0.5%, and a spectral index n_s = 0.965 +/- 0.004, which departs from exact scale invariance at more than eight sigma, as predicted. Primordial B-modes remain to be detected, but the scalar-sector evidence now firmly establishes the inflationary quantum origin of cosmic structure as a physical discovery.
